metadata.description: Lebanese Code of Commerce (1942), Companies Law, and related commercial legislation

laws.official_number: Legislative Decree of December 24, 1942 (Code of Commerce)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون التجارة البرية الصادر بتاريخ 24 كانون الأول 1942

laws.official_title_english: Code of Terrestrial Commerce / Code of Commerce

amendments.summary: Replaced the companies chapter of the Code of Commerce with a comprehensive modern companies law.

key_articles.text_english: Definition of commercial acts, merchant status, commercial register requirements.
key_articles.subject: Commercial acts and merchants

key_articles.text_english: Commercial books and accounting obligations for merchants.
key_articles.subject: Commercial books

key_articles.text_english: Negotiable instruments: bills of exchange, promissory notes, checks.
key_articles.subject: Negotiable instruments

laws.historical_context: Lebanon's commercial code was modeled closely on the French Commercial Code. Replaced the Ottoman Commercial Code (1850), itself a translation of the French Code de Commerce of 1807. Governs commercial transactions, merchant obligations, partnerships, negotiable instruments, bankruptcy, and commercial pledges. The companies chapter was replaced by Decree-Law 150/1983.

laws.official_title_arabic: مرسوم اشتراعي رقم 150 - قانون الشركات التجارية
laws.historical_context: Replaced the companies portion of the 1942 Code of Commerce. Governs formation, operation, and dissolution of all types of commercial companies: general partnerships (société en nom collectif), limited partnerships (société en commandite simple), joint stock companies (société anonyme / SAL), limited liability companies (société à responsabilité limitée / SARL), and holding companies (société holding). The SAL and SARL are the most common corporate forms in Lebanon.

Governs maritime commerce including ship registration, maritime liens, charter parties, bills of lading, maritime insurance, collisions, salvage, and general average. Important for Lebanon given the significance of the Port of Beirut to the national economy.

laws.official_number: Law No. 75 of April 3, 1967 (Intellectual Property / Copyright)
laws.official_title_arabic: قانون حماية الملكية الأدبية والفنية - قانون رقم 75/1967
laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 75/1967 sur la Protection de la Propriété Littéraire et Artistique
laws.official_title_english: Literary and Artistic Property Protection Law

amendments.summary: Updated copyright protections to align with international standards.

laws.historical_context: Lebanon's primary intellectual property legislation. Covers copyright, literary and artistic works, and neighboring rights. Lebanon is a member of the Berne Convention and TRIPS Agreement. Trademark protection is governed by separate legislation (Decree No. 2385 of 1924).

laws.official_title_french: Loi sur la Protection du Consommateur
laws.historical_context: Law No. 659/2005 established the consumer protection framework including product safety requirements, labeling, fair pricing, and established the Consumer Protection Directorate within the Ministry of Economy and Trade.

laws.official_number: Law No. 2/1967 (Trade Marks and Unfair Competition)
laws.official_title_french: Arrêté No. 2385/1924 et lois subséquentes - Marques de fabrique et de commerce
laws.official_title_english: Trademarks, Trade Names and Unfair Competition
laws.historical_context: Originally enacted as Decree No. 2385 of January 17, 1924, during the French Mandate. One of the oldest continuously enforced laws in Lebanon. Governs trademark registration, protection, and enforcement. Lebanon maintains a first-to-use system rather than first-to-file.
